InventoryItem.title: InventoryItem
InventoryItem.description: Represents an item in the inventory.

id.description: Unique identifier for the inventory item.

purchaseInvoiceNumber.description: The purchase invoice number associated with the item.

vendorName.description: The name of the vendor from whom the item was purchased.

date.description: The date the item was purchased.

itemStdCode.description: The standard code of the item.

itemCategory.description: The category of the item (e.g., Vehicle Part, Spare, Accessories).

quantity.description: The quantity of the item in stock.

storageLocation.description: The location where the item is stored.

unitPrice.description: The unit price of the item.

itemStatus.description: The current status of the item (e.g., In Stock, Sold, Damaged).

salesInvoiceNumber.description: The sales invoice number associated with the item, if any.

definition.description: Stores inventory items owned by a specific user. The path enforces ownership of inventory items by user ID. Only the user with the matching {userId} can access the inventory items in this collection. Includes denormalized 'userId' for authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The ID of the user who owns the inventory items.

params.name: itemId
params.description: The ID of the inventory item.

definition.description: Collection to store administrator role assignments.  The existence of a document with a user's ID in this collection grants them administrator privileges.

params.name: userId
params.description: The ID of the user who has admin role.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to manage inventory items with a focus on clear authorization and data integrity. It leverages path-based ownership for user-specific data and a dedicated collection for global role assignments, ensuring Authorization Independence (CRITICAL) and secure 'list' operations. The structure enforces invariants like ownership by storing the inventory items within a user-specific subcollection (`/users/{userId}/inventory_items/{itemId}`).

Specifically:

1.  **Authorization Independence:** There is no need for `get()` calls in security rules because access to inventory items is implicitly granted to the owner (the user whose `userId` matches `request.auth.uid`).
2.  **Clarity of Intent:** The path `/users/{userId}/inventory_items/{itemId}` clearly signifies that inventory items belong to a specific user.
3.  **DBAC (No Custom Claims):** Roles are managed via the `/roles_admin/{uid}` collection.
4.  **QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** Secure `list` operations are supported. Only the authenticated user can access their inventory items.
5.  **Invariants:** The structure ensures the integrity of ownership, as only the authenticated user can create, read, update, or delete inventory items within their specific path.
